sevenStepDecisions: Listening: identify an involuntary lapse and recovery in a map briefing, without inferring refusal or sleep.
Reply: explain a long-briefing lapse to a manager and suggest an agenda, pause, or recap; all four replies are usable.
Scene: classify a gallery inventory lapse with recorded recovery rather than deliberate omission or only topical drift.
Contrast: distinguish a discussion changing topic from a reader or volunteer losing focus.
Dialogue: repeat the specifically missed instruction without attributing misconduct to a trainee.
Speaking: describe returning to the last numbered recipe instruction after a lapse.
Writing: redesign an online first-aid training diagram for volunteers who reported attention lapses; shorter sections, checks and a return point are grounded in the prompt.
